findings.failure_scenario: For any execution part containing a shaped ALLOCATE (e.g. `allocate(a(n))`), `shape.children` yields `Allocate_Shape_Spec` objects (see ast_components.py:283-287, where the shape-spec visitor unpacks (lower, upper) from exactly these nodes); `_inject_knowns` falls through to its final `else: raise NotImplementedError`. The Execution_Part loop of `_track_local_consts` (line ~2337) catches NotImplementedError and executes `plus, minus = {}, set()`, so constants known before the allocate (e.g. `n = 4`) are no longer propagated to later statements — a regression versus the previous `(Allocate_Stmt, Deallocate_Stmt): pass` branch, which retained them — while the newly added allocation-bound injection does nothing.
findings.summary: The new Allocate_Stmt branch calls `_inject_knowns` on fparser `Allocate_Shape_Spec` nodes (the shape list's children), which that function does not handle and raises NotImplementedError for, so the intended injection never runs and the exception silently wipes the tracked local constants.

findings.failure_scenario: For an SDFG whose generated init code dereferences an array/struct argument — exactly the init code this PR's `add_deferred_shape_assigns_for_structs` emits (`sdfg.append_init_code(f"{newsize} = {name}->{size.name}")`, fortran_parser.py:180/211) — `csdfg.initialize(cfg=cfg, c=c)` constructs `initargs` from `_free_symbols` only (in the new un-skipped test there are no free symbols at all), so `__dace_init` is invoked with no/§ mispositioned arguments while the C signature (framecode.py:250, `sdfg.signature(arglist=self.arglist)`) expects `(cfg, c)`; the init code then dereferences a bogus pointer and segfaults. `__call__` works only because of the changed line, and `initargtuple` is now computed and unused in `__call__`.
findings.summary: `__call__` now passes the full argument tuple to `__dace_init_*`, but `initialize()` (line 359-360) still passes the symbols-only tuple from `_construct_args`, so the two initialization paths hand different argument lists to the same generated init function and one of them is wrong.

findings.failure_scenario: Two .ti entries with the same type/component but different scopes and values, e.g. `{... "root": "m.config_type", "component": "nlev", "scope": "mod_a", "value": "4"}` and the same with `"scope": "mod_b", "value": "8"`, now hit `assert inj_map[key].value == x.value` and raise `AssertionError: Inconsistent values in constant injections...`, aborting `ecrad_config_injection_list()`/`find_all_config_injections` and every SDFG build that loads those files, instead of yielding both scope-restricted injections. Values are compared as raw JSON strings, so semantically equal spellings ("0" vs "0.0") also trip it.
findings.summary: The new deduplication key `(root, comp)` ignores `scope_spec`, which is part of a ConstInjection's identity, so injections that differ only in scope are conflated and can abort loading with an assertion.

findings.failure_scenario: `_instance_injection_applies_to_instance` (ast_desugaring.py:3283-3296) explicitly matches component paths by length and prefix (`len(comp_spec) != len(item.component_spec)` / `comp_spec[:-1] != item.component_spec[:-1]`), so a .ti entry of type ConstInstanceInjection with a dotted component (e.g. "component": "cfg.a") previously matched and its value was propagated. After this change it is skipped at load time with only a stderr message, so that constant is no longer injected anywhere and the generated SDFG silently differs.
findings.summary: The new `len(component_spec) > 1` guard silently drops multi-level component specs for ConstInstanceInjection as well, although the instance-matching code supports them.

findings.failure_scenario: `find_type_of_entity` returns `('CHARACTER',)` for `character`/`character(len=n)` entities (ast_desugaring.py:775-795). When such an entity is an allocatable component with a `:` shape and matching `__f2dace_SA_/_SOA_` injections, the injection path calls `typ.to_decl(name)` (line 3479) and the declaration is regenerated as `type(CHARACTER), dimension(3)` instead of `CHARACTER, dimension(3)`; `Type_Declaration_Stmt(nudecl)` then fails to parse / invalid Fortran is produced. Before the change the identity fallback emitted a valid `CHARACTER`.
findings.summary: Changing the TYPE_MAP fallback from the identity to `f"type({typ})"` wraps every intrinsic type name that is not in TYPE_MAP — notably CHARACTER — into an invalid declaration.

findings.failure_scenario: For a named interface, `identifier_specs` maps its spec to the Interface_Stmt itself, so the loop condition `isinstance(v, Interface_Stmt)` subtracts it; for an anonymous interface block, the key is the spec of the contained Function_Stmt/Subroutine_Stmt, whose `v.parent.parent` is the Interface_Block, so it is subtracted too. The set is therefore empty and uncalled interface blocks are never removed by `remove_self(alias_map[ui].parent)` — the pipeline still relies on other passes and can end in `RuntimeError: Could not remove all the interfaces from AST` (fortran_parser.py:2844-2846). If a spec ever were missing from `alias_map`, `assert ui in alias_map` aborts the frontend instead.
findings.summary: `unused_ifaces` is seeded with every interface spec and then has every interface that appears in `alias_map` subtracted, which is all of them, so the removal loop at line 1510 can never execute.

findings.failure_scenario: `create_singular_sdfg_from_string(..., config_injections=[ConstTypeInjection(None, ('lib','config'), ('cfg','field'), '3')])` (the public API used by tests and by external users; the .ti format itself allows dotted components) now aborts the frontend with `AssertionError: Unimplemented: type injection must have just one-level of component for now...`, whereas before the change it printed the same message to stderr and simply skipped that injection (as the new loader-level filter in config_propagation_data.py does for file-loaded ones).
findings.summary: `_type_injection_applies_to_component` now asserts single-level component specs, turning previously-tolerated input into a hard failure for callers that pass injections programmatically rather than through the filtering loader.
